why_it_matters: A restore drill without named authority can expose data or create unclear accountability.
evidence_to_capture: Client, protected system, data owner, test owner, approver, purpose, and test date
test_method: Confirm the approver and data owner accept the exact system, destination, and test window before work begins.

why_it_matters: File, application, image, and full-system restores require different evidence and dependencies.
evidence_to_capture: Recovery type, protected scope, exclusions, and success definition
test_method: Select one recovery type and confirm the requested source and destination match it.

control: Set recovery point and time targets
why_it_matters: A completed restore cannot be evaluated without an expected data-loss window and usable-recovery time.
evidence_to_capture: RPO, RTO, measurement start and stop, and acceptance evidence
test_method: Calculate the newest acceptable recovery point and define when the restored service becomes usable.

why_it_matters: A poorly isolated test can overwrite production data or expose recovered information.
evidence_to_capture: Destination, isolation control, capacity check, network boundary, and cleanup owner
test_method: Attempt to reach production write paths from the test destination and confirm the approved boundary holds.

why_it_matters: Testing an arbitrary snapshot may not prove the actual protected workload can be recovered.
evidence_to_capture: Recovery-point timestamp, job ID, retention tier, source endpoint, and protected scope
test_method: Select a dated recovery point that represents the workload and reconcile it to the protected-source inventory.

why_it_matters: Unresolved warnings or missing sources can invalidate the selected recovery point.
evidence_to_capture: Job status, warnings, missing items, credential state, and retention exceptions
test_method: Inspect the source job and stop if a warning affects the data or system being tested.

why_it_matters: Expected hashes, sizes, owners, and application meaning allow the restored result to be tested objectively.
evidence_to_capture: Artifact list with expected hash, size, date, owner, permissions, and purpose
test_method: Select representative files or objects and record their expected properties before restoration.

why_it_matters: Recovery may fail even when data exists if credentials, keys, approvals, or network paths are unavailable.
evidence_to_capture: Encryption key reference, MFA path, approvals, network access, and technician role
test_method: Verify every required dependency through the approved path without copying secrets into the record.

why_it_matters: Actor, source, destination, timing, and job identifiers are needed for audit and reconstruction.
evidence_to_capture: Actor, source, destination, selected items, start time, and restore job ID
test_method: Start through the approved workflow and confirm the audit record matches the request.

why_it_matters: Restoring into production by default increases overwrite and availability risk.
evidence_to_capture: Recovery folder, isolated host or sandbox, network controls, and approved exception if in place
test_method: Restore to a separate location and confirm the protected source remains unchanged.

why_it_matters: Tenant, endpoint, point, destination, permission, or item-count mismatches can turn a drill into an incident.
evidence_to_capture: Expected and observed scope plus stop decision
test_method: Introduce or detect a scope mismatch and confirm the operator stops before data is written.

why_it_matters: Retries, throttling, warnings, and manual intervention affect repeatability and recovery timing.
evidence_to_capture: Progress log, warnings, retries, transfer rate, failures, completion time, and interventions
test_method: Run the restore and preserve the complete execution timeline without sensitive content.

why_it_matters: Presence alone does not prove that the expected scope was recovered completely.
evidence_to_capture: Expected and actual counts, sizes, timestamps, paths, and missing items
test_method: Compare restored files or objects with the approved manifest and investigate every difference.

why_it_matters: A restore can complete while recovered content is corrupted or different from the source.
evidence_to_capture: Expected and actual hashes or another integrity signal
test_method: Calculate and compare hashes for representative content where the data type permits it.

why_it_matters: A file that exists but cannot be opened or interpreted is not a usable recovery.
evidence_to_capture: Application used, validation step, observed result, and tester
test_method: Open representative content or start the isolated application workflow and record whether it behaves as expected.

why_it_matters: Incorrect ownership, ACLs, encryption, metadata, links, or dependencies can make restored data unusable or unsafe.
evidence_to_capture: Owner, ACL, inheritance, encryption state, metadata, links, and dependency results
test_method: Compare restored access and dependency behavior with the approved expected state.

why_it_matters: Queue time, transfer time, repair, and application validation all affect the real recovery path.
evidence_to_capture: Authorized start, queue, transfer, repair, validation, usable time, and total duration
test_method: Calculate total elapsed time and each component against the defined RTO.

why_it_matters: A successful restore may still exceed the acceptable data-loss window.
evidence_to_capture: Recovery-point timestamp, incident or test reference time, age, and RPO variance
test_method: Calculate the recovered point's age and explain any excluded or stale source.

why_it_matters: Runbooks and contact lists are unproven until a failed dependency is escalated successfully.
evidence_to_capture: Escalation path, support contact, alternate media, credential recovery, response, and outcome
test_method: Trigger a safe dependency failure and confirm the documented escalation path works.

why_it_matters: Bandwidth, storage, egress, licensing, and operational bottlenecks can block recovery at incident scale.
evidence_to_capture: Observed throughput, storage use, egress, license constraints, bottlenecks, and cost evidence
test_method: Compare the test footprint with the expected incident scale and record material limits.

why_it_matters: Recovered data left in a test location creates unnecessary security and privacy exposure.
evidence_to_capture: Cleanup authorization, deleted paths, disposal method, completion time, and verifier
test_method: Remove the test copy under the approved procedure and confirm the protected source remains intact.

why_it_matters: Failed, slow, partial, inaccessible, or unverifiable outcomes require a risk owner and retest path.
evidence_to_capture: Finding, affected scope, risk, compensating control, owner, due date, and retest condition
test_method: Convert every failed or conditional result into an owned record and reject unowned exceptions.

why_it_matters: A test creates value only when observed dependencies and corrections improve the next recovery.
evidence_to_capture: Runbook revision, scope change, credential or contact update, capacity change, and cadence
test_method: Repeat the documented procedure from the revised runbook and confirm another operator can follow it.

control: Approve closure and schedule the next test
why_it_matters: A green job status is not closure without accepted evidence, disposed test data, and a future validation date.
evidence_to_capture: Approver, decision, open exceptions, disposal confirmation, next test date, and acceptance date
test_method: Review the evidence pack with the approver and close only when exceptions are owned and the next drill is scheduled.
